Groove — Trade Information

A memoir of depression, generational trauma, and the sheer stubbornness of survival — and everything booksellers need to stock it.

Download the sell sheet (PDF) Email the author

"I booked a one-way trip to Tahiti I never meant to come back from. Groove is the story of why I came back."

From the outside, her life looked successful — a senior engineer at a major tech company, a loving family, a home far from where she started. Inside, she was being consumed by a depression no one around her could see.

Groove is part confession, part atonement, part love letter to the sheer stubbornness of survival. A raw and fiercely honest account of moving through the world — the wounds we inherit, the ruts we get stuck in, and the groove we learn to move in. Unflinching, funny at the very edge of grief, and ultimately a survivor's account that leaves readers lighter than it found them.

"The pictures were real. I just wasn't in any of them anymore."

For readers of Kiese Laymon's Heavy and Glennon Doyle's Untamed.

Why it sells

01

Depression hiding in plain sight

Flips the stereotype — a high-achiever no one knew was struggling. The kind of recognition readers hand to a friend.

02

A voice readers rarely get

A debut memoir from a Black woman in STEM — intimate, culturally rooted, and sharp.

03

Hard truth, real hope

Honest about suicide and inherited pain, but it's a book about staying — and the way back.

04

Short, literary & giftable

108 pages with original etching-style illustrations — a book made to be held and passed along.
